whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: California's Two-Year Filing Window
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the incident, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can mean losing your right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help sort out how fault is divided.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses. That means your recovery isn't artificially capped the way it is in some other states.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you don't pay unless they win money for you. This makes it possible to get legal help without any upfront cost.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Dorris?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the incident to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity was involved, the notice period can be as short as six months, so it's best not to wait.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly at fault doesn't stop you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault, which an attorney can help evaluate.
